## Purpose

Return the current stuck-task list without changing work. Each row includes
project, task ID, state, elapsed seconds, reason and a suggested diagnostic
command. `summary` formats the same rows as one line per task.

## When a playbook uses it

The system `stuck-task-watch` calls it every ten minutes, ends on an empty
`stuck` list, and otherwise sends `summary` to `session:supervisor-global` via
`message_send`. Repeated nonempty ticks intentionally repeat the notification.

## How it works internally

`SystemCommandsMixin._cmd_get_stuck_tasks` reads a task/worker/hold snapshot
through `src/database/queries/stall_watch_queries.py`. `src/stall_watch.py`
checks aged active tasks, orphaned workers after 20 minutes and unroutable
READY tasks after 30 minutes. READY causes come from canonical task explain.
Paused projects, containers and human holds are excluded. See the
[watch specification](../../specs/stuck-task-watch.md) for thresholds.

## Side effects and persistence

None. The command neither repairs tasks nor writes messages or watch memory.
The playbook decides when to call the separate messaging command.

## Failure modes and diagnostics

`rejected` reports an out-of-scope project or a failed task explanation read.
Unexpected read failures end the playbook step with `runtime_error`. Inspect
the failed run and use `aq task explain --task-id <id>` for individual tasks.
The next timer tick attempts a new observation.

## Example step

Call `get_stuck_tasks` with no arguments and bind the `read` result as `watch`.
If `watch.stuck` is nonempty, send `watch.summary` to the global supervisor.
An optional `project_id` narrows the observation for other callers.
